What each column of a registered schema means

Source: R/crt_schema_cols.R
crt_schema_cols.Rd

Returns the schema's column declarations as a tibble, one row per column in schema order: type, whether it is required, and what the schema says the column means, including the allowed values a QC rule can check a record against.

Usage

crt_schema_cols(source, file_name)

Arguments

source

Character. Source family code (e.g. "nge").

file_name

Character. Logical file name (e.g. "form_pscis").

Value

A tibble with columns:

name, type, required

as declared; see crt_schema_conform()

units

unit of a measurement, e.g. "m", else NA

values

list of character vectors: the values the column may store, or character(0) when the schema sets none

labels

list of character vectors, parallel to values: what a form displays for each. The same as values unless the vocabulary is coded, e.g. stores "4" and displays "Coniferous Trees"

range_min, range_max

numeric bounds, else NA

relative_to

for a column holding file paths, what they are relative to, else NA

null

what a null means in this column when it means something other than "not recorded", else NA

notes

the schema's description of the column, else NA

Details

This is the reading of a schema meant for other code. A form builder takes the column list, types and vocabularies from here and adds only how the form shows them; a QC rule takes values and range_min / range_max and flags a record whose value falls outside them. Neither has to parse the YAML.

values and the range are declarations, not checks: crt_schema_conform() does not refuse a value outside them. A value typed or dictated outside a vocabulary is a record to flag, not one to drop.

See also

crt_schema_grade() for which records can answer a question, crt_files() to list registered entries.

Examples

cols <- crt_schema_cols("nge", "form_capture")
cols[, c("name", "type", "required")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   name           type     required
#>   <chr>          <chr>    <lgl>   
#> 1 project        string   TRUE    
#> 2 form           string   TRUE    
#> 3 record_id      integer  TRUE    
#> 4 source_version string   TRUE    
#> 5 schema_version string   TRUE    
#> 6 captured_at    datetime TRUE
